newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FAI says still sees better year profit.
newsitem.headline: FAI says still sees better year profit.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd chief executive Rodney Adler said on Wednesday FAI still expected a better profit in 1996/97 (July-June), although its expectations had been diminished in the past few months.
But the increase would be "nothing like" the 35.4 percent profit rise to achieved in the first half ending December 31.

"Our (full year) profit expectations at the half year have been diminished in the last few months, mainly because of the operations of our coal company, due to the falling coal price and higher Australian dollar," Adler told reporters.
FAI reported a net profit of A$7.7 million for the six months to December 31.
FAI said in its half year results that the contribution from its wholly-owned Oceanic Coal Australia Ltd was lower due to the geology of the area now being mined.
FAI reported a net profit of A$10.04 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
FAI shares were three cents firmer at 65 cents at 2.40 p.m. (0440 GMT).
